text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: RED ALERT — P99 streaming latency spike for customer 'saffron' on hosted API. Route: /v1/stream/generate. p95 jumped to ~4.5s, p99 spiked to ~18.4s, streaming stall rate ~8.7%. Started 1945678860.

maria: paging @oncall — saffron is single-tenant heavy; customer complaining about stalls. can you take? :eyes:

oncall: i'm taking this. joining prod dashboard now. what's the initial blast radius?

ashwin: seeing high concurrent sessions from saffron (burst ~900 concurrent). normal is ~80. possible prompt storm + long contexts. CPU/GPU queues backing up.

lenora: please check streaming chunk latency traces and kvcache evictions. last time long prefixes caused thrash.

kai: grabbing logs. running quick grep to identify failing streamers:
```
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=streamer -c streamer --tail=200 | grep saffron | sed -n '1,120p'
```

kai: sample errors show repeated stalled forward passes and kvcache-miss spikes: 
```
2026-03-14T15:01:12Z streamer[pid]: shard=3 session=saffron-abc stall=streaming_send_timeout
2026-03-14T15:01:13Z streamer[pid]: kvcache_evictions=423 read_latency_ms=12.9
2026-03-14T15:01:14Z modelrunner[pid]: queue_wait_ms=1034 batch_size=16
```

maria: propose immediate mitigations: 1) throttle saffron concurrency to 25; 2) route saffron to dedicated pool 'dedi-saffron' if available; 3) enable streaming fallback (no-chunk) to reduce overhead. Thoughts?

oncall: agreed. doing (1) now. applying temporary rate-limit policy. command: 
```
redwoodctl policy create --customer saffron --type concurrency --limit 25 --scope streaming-temp-2026-03-14
```

oncall: policy applied, response id=plc_01F8.

ashwin: create routing fallback meanwhile. checking if dedi pool has capacity. 

lenora: dedi pool shows spare GPUs in eu-west-1. if we route, we should also reduce model size for saffron to raven-3b-quant fallback to cut inference time.

oncall: routing canary started: 
```
redwoodctl route set --customer saffron --to pool=dedi-saffron --percent=10 --model_fallback=raven-3b-quant
```

oncall: canary accepted. monitoring p95/p99.

sre-manager: Also open temporary autoscale bump for streamer replicas to handle prefix fanout until we confirm root cause. I'll approve if needed.

kai: metrics after throttle+canary (1m window): p95 -> 1.8s (was 4.5s), p99 -> 2.6s (was 18.4s), stall rate -> 2.4% (was 8.7%). looks like throttling helped a lot.

maria: nice — that confirms overload from concurrency plus long prompts. we should still investigate why kvcache thrash happens at this scale. add to postmortem.

lenora: quick root cause notes: saffron's sdk push sent many large multi-shot prompts (avg tokens per request ~7400) and very high session churn. our kvcache per-shard eviction policy is suboptimal for >8k token prefixes under high concurrency.

ashwin: follow-ups: 1) implement prompt-length-based routing rule (if prompt_tokens > 4k -> route to dedicated/large-kv nodes) 2) improve kvcache eviction heuristic 3) product to talk to saffron about client throttling and batching.

maria: creating incident ticket and assigning postmortem. owner: @lenora. sev: high, impact: single-tenant but production affecting streaming SLA.

oncall: handing off live watch to @ashwin for next 30m while I eat. pls monitor dedicated pool thrash and any error regressions.

ashwin: taking watch. I'll keep refresh on alerts and metrics. if p99 creeps back above 5s, escalate to infra-scaling and consider temporarily disabling streaming for saffron.

sre-manager: filed follow-up tasks: PM-4762 (routing rule), INF-4421 (kvcache heuristic), CUST-881 (customer contact). please add logs/traces to the ticket.

incident-bot: incident created: INC-2026-03-14-1945678901, severity=high, impacted_customers=["saffron"]. automated postmortem flag set to true.

maria: thanks team. good mitigation work. we'll draft a short customer note for saffron and schedule a technical review. :thumbsup:

oncall: backbrief in #postmortems in 1h. closing urgent loop.

ashwin: monitoring continues. p99 steady ~2.3s at 1945678980. handing off to next shift for follow-up.

lenora: adding pointer to traces and example long prompt in the ticket.

maria: closing thread for active mitigation — keep updates in the incident ticket.
